label: Bees kill most of their kings to prevent the hive splitting
statement: Worker bees kill most of their kings, especially inferior ones, to prevent a multiplicity of kings from splitting the hive, and destroy royal cells when no swarm is intended.
quote: These bees also kill without mercy most of their kings, and especially kings of the inferior sort; and this they do for fear a multiplicity of kings should lead to a dismemberment of the hive.

label: On each trip a bee visits flowers of only one kind
statement: On each foraging trip a bee goes from flower to flower of one kind only and does not visit another kind until it has returned to the hive.
quote: On each expedition the bee does not fly from a flower of one kind to a flower of another, but flies from one violet, say, to another violet, and never meddles with another flower until it has got back to the hive

label: The most children a woman has borne at one birth is five
statement: The largest number of children ever born to a woman at one birth is five, which has been observed several times.
quote: The largest number ever brought forth is five, and such an occurrence has been witnessed on several occasions.

label: Older bees work indoors, younger bees forage outside
statement: Older bees do the work inside the hive and are rough and hairy from staying indoors, while young bees do the carrying outside and are comparatively smooth.
quote: The elder bees do the indoor work, and are rough and hairy from staying indoors; the young bees do the outer carrying, and are comparatively smooth.

label: Selachians lack gill covers because their skeleton is cartilage
statement: In most fishes the gills are covered by opercula, but selachians (cartilaginous fishes) have none, because their skeleton is cartilaginous.
quote: These gills are in most fishes covered by opercula, but in the Selachia, owing to the skeleton being cartilaginous, there are no such coverings.

label: Horned animals are mostly cloven-hoofed; none is solid-hoofed with two horns
statement: The great majority of horned animals are cloven-hoofed, and no solid-hoofed animal with a pair of horns has ever been found.
quote: The great majority of the horned animals are cloven-footed, as the ox, the stag, the goat; and a solid-hooved animal with a pair of horns has never yet been met with.

label: The dolphin has two breasts near its genitals
statement: The dolphin bears live young directly and has two breasts placed near its genitals rather than high up, with no visible teats but two slits from which milk flows.
quote: Thus the dolphin is directly viviparous, and accordingly we find it furnished with two breasts, not situated high up, but in the neighbourhood of the genitals.

label: In insects the female inserts her organ into the male
statement: In copulating insects the female pushes her sexual organ up into the body of the male, the reverse of what happens in other animals.
quote: The female pushes from underneath her sexual organ into the body of the male above, this being the reverse of the operation observed in other creatures
scope: insects, e.g. flies and cantharid beetles

label: All hair-coated animals are viviparous
statement: Every animal with a coat of hair (counting the spines of hedgehogs and porcupines as hair) bears live young.
quote: All animals, however, that are hair-coated are viviparous.

label: Elephant gestation lasts two years with a single calf
statement: The female elephant carries her young for two years and bears only one at a time.
quote: The period of gestation with the female is two years; and only one young animal is produced at a time, in other words it is uniparous.

label: The male sheat-fish guards the spawn for forty to fifty days
statement: In the sheat-fish the female leaves after spawning while the male guards the spawn and fry, driving off small fish, for forty or fifty days until the young can escape on their own.
quote: contenting himself with keeping off all other little fishes that might steal the spawn or fry, and this he does for forty or fifty days, until the young are sufficiently grown to make away from the other fishes for themselves.

label: Eels arise from 'earth's guts' in mud and wet ground
statement: Eels arise from the so-called 'earth's guts', worms that grow spontaneously in mud and humid ground where sun heat causes putrefaction.
quote: Eels are derived from the so-called 'earth's guts' that grow spontaneously in mud and in humid ground

label: Only male cicadas sing
statement: In both the large and small cicadas it is the male that sings and the female is silent.
quote: In both species, the larger and the smaller, it is the male that sings, and the female that is unvocal.

label: Rabies passes to every animal bitten by a mad dog except man
statement: Rabies drives dogs mad and is fatal to them, and any animal bitten by a rabid dog catches it and dies, with the exception of man.
quote: ary animal whatever, excepting man, will take the disease if bitten by a dog so afflicted; the disease is fatal to the dog itself, and to any animal it may bite, man excepted.

label: Hair goes on growing after death
statement: Hair continues to grow after death, though it does not begin growing then.
quote: Hair actually goes on growing after death; it does not, however, begin growing then.

label: Males have more teeth than females in man, sheep, goats and swine
statement: In men, sheep, goats and swine, males have more teeth than females.
quote: Males have more teeth than females in the case of men, sheep, goats, and swine

label: Of all hybrids only mules are sterile
statement: Animals born of crosses between different kinds can all mate and produce young of both sexes, except mules, which alone are sterile.
quote: Of the animals that arise from such union all except mules are found to copulate again with each other and to be able to produce young of both sexes, but mules alone are sterile
scope: Hybrids between related kinds (dogs, foxes, wolves, partridges and hens, hawks, rays), contrasted with mules

label: Semen does not come from all parts of the body
statement: Semen is not drawn from every part of the parent's body, contrary to those who explain inheritance that way.
quote: Into this we must next inquire, since it is plain that the semen is not secreted from all the parts.

label: Partridge hens feign lameness to lure intruders from the brood
statement: When a man comes upon a partridge brood, the hen rolls in front of him pretending to be lame, drawing him away until the young have escaped, then returns and calls them back.
quote: When a man comes by chance upon a young brood, and tries to catch them, the hen-bird rolls in front of the hunter, pretending to be lame: the man every moment thinks he is on the point of catching her, and so she draws him on and on, until every one of her brood has had time to escape

label: Fish are prolific because most of their eggs are destroyed
statement: Most fish eggs that are laid are destroyed before hatching, and fish produce great numbers of eggs to make up for this loss.
quote: even as it is most of those laid are destroyed before hatching. Hence the class of fish is prolific, for Nature makes up for the destruction by numbers.

label: All cephalopods have eight feet, short in cuttlefish and squid, long in octopus
statement: All cephalopods have eight feet, which are short in cuttlefish and squid and longer in the octopus.
quote: Again, though the number of feet is the same in all the Cephalopoda, namely eight, their length varies in different kinds, being short in the Sepias and the Calamaries, but greater in the Poulps.

label: The she-bear gives birth during winter concealment and emerges in spring
statement: The she-bear gives birth while in winter concealment and stays hidden until she brings the cubs out in spring, about three months after the winter solstice; bears eat nothing while hidden.
quote: The female brings forth her young at this time, and remains in concealment until it is time to bring the cubs out; and she brings them out in spring, about three months after the winter solstice.

label: Scaly fish lay eggs; cartilaginous fish bear live young
statement: Scaly fishes are always oviparous, and cartilaginous fishes are all viviparous except the fishing-frog.
quote: scaly fish are invariably oviparous, but cartilaginous fishes are all viviparous, with the single exception of the fishing-frog.
scope: Scaly (bony) fishes and selachians (cartilaginous fishes); the fishing-frog (anglerfish, Lophius)

label: Eels have no milt, spawn or reproductive passages
statement: Eels are neither born from pairing nor oviparous: no eel has ever been found with milt or spawn, nor with passages for spawn or eggs.
quote: nor was an eel ever found supplied with either milt or spawn, nor are they when cut open found to have within them passages for spawn or for eggs

label: Some cartilaginous fishes complete development by connection to the uterus
statement: In some cartilaginous fishes, once the nutriment of the egg is used up, the embryo completes its development by connection with the uterus, so the egg is not released from the uterus.
quote: in other cases, when the nutriment from the egg is consumed, development is completed by connection with the uterus, and therefore the egg is not set free from the uterus.
scope: Selachians (cartilaginous fishes), e.g. placental sharks such as the smooth dogfish

label: Only humans visibly go grey with age, and to a lesser degree horses
statement: Humans go grey on the head as they age, but this is not visible in practically any other animal except, to some extent, the horse.
quote: Human beings also go grey on the head as they grow old, but this is not visible in practically any other animal, though more so in the horse than others.

label: The argonaut uses its web as a sail and arms as oars
statement: The nautilus (argonaut) rises to the surface and, when a breeze blows, uses a thin web between its arms as a sail and lets down some arms as rudder-oars.
quote: It uses this structure, when a breeze is blowing, for a sail, and lets down some of its feelers alongside as rudder-oars.

label: Ichneumon wasps provision mud-sealed holes with dead spiders
statement: The wasps called ichneumons, smaller than ordinary wasps, kill spiders, carry them to a hole in a wall, seal it with mud and lay their grubs inside, and from the grubs come new ichneumons.
quote: kill spiders and carry off the dead bodies to a wall or some such place with a hole in it; this hole they smear over with mud and lay their grubs inside it, and from the grubs come the hunter-wasps

label: Man has eight ribs on each side
statement: The human trunk has eight ribs on each side.
quote: Common to the upper and lower part of the trunk are the 'ribs', eight on either side

label: A female partridge downwind of the male becomes impregnated
statement: A female partridge becomes impregnated if she gets to leeward of the male, and often merely by hearing his voice or by his breathing on her as he flies overhead.
quote: With partridges, by the way, if the female gets to leeward of the male, she becomes thereby impregnated.

label: The right kidney lies higher than the left in all animals
statement: In all animals that have kidneys, the right kidney lies higher in the body than the left.
quote: In all animals that are provided with this organ, the right kidney is situated higher up than the other.

label: Bee kings generate both kings and workers
statement: The 'kings' (leaders) of a hive generate both their own kind and the worker bees.
quote: since those occupied with the tendance of these creatures deny this, it remains that the kings must generate both their own kind and the bees.
scope: the honey bee (Apis mellifera); 'kings' are queens

label: Swans sing chiefly as they approach death
statement: Swans are musical and sing chiefly at the approach of death, flying out to sea at that time.
quote: They are musical, and sing chiefly at the approach of death; at this time they fly out to sea, and men, when sailing past the coast of Libya, have fallen in with many of them out at sea singing in mournful strains

label: Elephants breathe through the raised trunk when crossing water
statement: Elephants, being both land and swamp animals, have a lengthened nostril which, when they traverse water, they lift above the surface and breathe through, like a diver's breathing instrument.
quote: so also have elephants been furnished by nature with their lengthened nostril; and, whenever they have to traverse the water, they lift this up above the surface and breathe through it.

label: Man has the largest and moistest brain for his size
statement: Relative to body size, man has the largest and the moistest brain of any animal.
quote: But, taking size for size of animal, the largest brain, and the moistest, is that of man.
scope: Man compared with all other animals that have a brain

label: Worker wasps all die in winter; only the mother-wasps overwinter
statement: Worker wasps do not survive into a second year but all die as winter comes on, while the larger mother-wasps survive the winter in holes underground.
quote: The workers do not live over into a second year, but all die when winter comes on; and this can be proved, for at the commencement of winter the workers become drowsy, and about the time of the winter solstice they are never seen at all.

label: The brooding female octopus stops feeding and loses condition
statement: The female octopus, after laying her eggs, broods over them and loses condition because she does not go out for food during the hatching period.
quote: The female, after laying her eggs, broods over them, and in consequence gets out of condition, by reason of not going in quest of food during the hatching period.

label: A bee that stings dies because it loses its gut with the sting
statement: A bee that stings dies because it cannot withdraw its sting without tearing out its intestines; once it loses its sting it must die.
quote: Bees that sting die from their inability to extract the sting without at the same time extracting their intestines.

label: The crocodile moves its upper jaw rather than its lower
statement: In all other animals it is the lower jaw that moves, but in the river crocodile it is the upper jaw.
quote: While in all other animals it is the lower jaw that is movable, in the river crocodile it is exceptionally the upper.
scope: the Nile crocodile versus other animals

label: Crustaceans moult not once but repeatedly
statement: Crabs, crawfish and lobsters slough their shells, becoming soft all over, and they do so not once for all but over and over again.
quote: These animals also do not cast their skins once and for all, but over and over again.

label: Eels go down from rivers to the sea while mullet go up
statement: The mullet migrates up from the sea into marshes and rivers, while eels migrate down from marshes and rivers to the sea.
quote: The mullet goes up from the sea to marshes and rivers; the eels, on the contrary, make their way down from the marshes and rivers to the sea.

label: Young scorpions and spiders kill their parent after hatching
statement: When the land-scorpion's brood has hatched, the young eject and kill the parent, as also happens with the spider.
quote: When the hatching is completed, the parent animal, as happens with the parent spider, is ejected and put to death by the young ones

label: Snakes and lizards hide for four months in winter and eat nothing
statement: Scaly animals such as the serpent, lizard, gecko and river crocodile go into hiding for four months in the depth of winter and eat nothing during that time.
quote: all of which go into hiding for four months in the depth of winter, and during that time eat nothing.

label: All testaceans are spontaneously generated in mud, according to the material
statement: As a general rule all testaceans (shelled molluscs and the like) arise by spontaneous generation in mud, and differ according to the material: oysters in slime, cockles on sandy bottoms, ascidians, barnacles and limpets in rock hollows.
quote: As a general rule, then, all testaceans grow by spontaneous generation in mud, differing from one another according to the differences of the material
scope: testaceans: oysters, cockles, mussels, scallops, limpets, ascidians, barnacles

label: The ass alone among hairy animals has neither lice nor ticks
statement: All feathered and hair-coated animals are infested with lice, with the single exception of the ass, which has neither lice nor ticks.
quote: All other winged animals that are furnished with feathers are similarly infested, and all hair-coated creatures also, with the single exception of the ass, which is infested neither with lice nor with ticks.

label: The brain is bloodless, has no veins and is cold
statement: In all animals the brain is bloodless, has no veins in it and is naturally cold to the touch.
quote: The brain in all animals is bloodless, devoid of veins, and naturally cold to the touch

label: No bird with crooked talons is gregarious
statement: No bird with crooked talons (a bird of prey) lives in flocks.
quote: no bird furnished with crooked talons is gregarious
scope: Birds with hooked talons (raptors: eagles, hawks, falcons, owls, vultures)

label: Many birds hide in winter rather than migrate, including swallows
statement: Many birds do not migrate to warmer countries but hide where they are in winter; swallows have often been found in holes without feathers, and the kite, stork, turtle-dove, lark and others go into hiding.
quote: A great number of birds also go into hiding; they do not all migrate, as is generally supposed, to warmer countries.
scope: swallow, kite, stork, owzel, turtle-dove, lark, thrush, starling, owl

label: Erythrinus and channa are always caught full of eggs
statement: Fishes are mostly divided into males and females, but specimens of the erythrinus and the channa are never caught except full of eggs.
quote: Fishes for the most part are divided into males and females, but one is puzzled to account for the erythrinus and the channa, for specimens of these species are never caught except in a condition of pregnancy.
scope: channa (likely Serranus cabrilla) and erythrinus (a sea bream or serranid)

label: The cuckoo is not a transformed hawk
statement: The cuckoo is not a transformed hawk: it lacks the hawk's crooked talons, resembles the pigeon in head and claws, and is preyed on by hawks, which never happens between birds of one kind.
quote: The cuckoo has been seen to be preyed on by the hawk; and this never happens between birds of the same species.

label: All newborn children have bluish eyes that later change colour
statement: The eyes of all children are bluish at birth and later change to their permanent colour, which is not seen in other animals.
quote: The eyes of all children are bluish immediately after birth; later on they change to the colour which is to be theirs permanently. But in the case of other animals this is not visible.

label: Horned animals lacking upper front teeth have four stomachs and ruminate
statement: Horned quadrupeds that lack a full set of teeth in both jaws have a stomach of four chambers, and these are the animals that chew the cud.
quote: such of the horned animals as are not equally furnished with teeth in both jaws are furnished with four such chambers. These animals, by the way, are those that are said to chew the cud.

label: Resemblance can skip a generation and reappear in grandchildren
statement: Children usually resemble their parents or ancestors, but resemblance can be passed on after several generations, appearing in a grandchild but not in the child.
quote: While children mostly resemble their parents or their ancestors, it sometimes happens that no such resemblance is to be traced. But parents may pass on resemblance after several generations

label: The brain is insensible and not the cause of sensation
statement: The brain cannot be the cause of any sensation, being itself as without feeling as any of the excretions; the sensory centre is the region of the heart.
quote: and, as to the other half of their statement, the brain cannot be the cause of any of the sensations, seeing that it is itself as utterly without feeling as any one of the excretions.

label: The octopus arm inserted in the female's funnel is not a generative organ
statement: The arm that the male octopus inserts into the female's funnel serves only for attachment and is not an organ useful for generation, being outside the male's seminal passage.
quote: is only for the sake of attachment, and it is not an organ useful for generation, for it is outside the passage in the male and indeed outside the body of the male altogether.
scope: Octopus (poulp) and other cephalopods with a hectocotylus

label: Man lives longer than any animal except the elephant
statement: Man lives longer than any animal for which there is credible evidence, except the elephant.
quote: Man lives a longer time than any animal of which we have any credible experience except the elephant
scope: humans compared with other animals, especially mammals

label: Pigeons pair for life
statement: Pigeons pair with the same mate until one of the pair dies, though occasionally a female mates with a bird other than her mate.
quote: In pairing the same male and the same female keep together; and the union is only broken by the death of one of the two parties.
scope: pigeons and doves (tame pigeon, ring-dove, turtle-dove)

label: No animal has both tusks and horns, nor does any saw-toothed animal
statement: No animal has both tusks and horns, and no animal with interlocking pointed (saw-like) teeth has either tusks or horns.
quote: No animal is there that possesses both tusks and horns, nor yet do either of these structures exist in any animal possessed of 'saw-teeth'.

label: The halcyon breeds at the winter solstice
statement: The halcyon (kingfisher) breeds at the time of the winter solstice, unlike nearly all other birds, which breed in spring and early summer.
quote: The halcyon breeds at the season of the winter solstice.
scope: the halcyon (usually identified as the common kingfisher)

label: Stationary testaceans and attached animals have no sexes
statement: Animals that do not move about, such as testaceans (shelled molluscs and the like) and animals that live clinging to something, have no sexes, any more than plants do.
quote: But all those creatures which do not move, as the testacea and animals that live by clinging to something else, inasmuch as their nature resembles that of plants, have no sex any more than plants have
scope: Sessile animals: testaceans (bivalves, sea snails and the like) and attached animals (sponges, sea squirts, barnacles)

label: The torpedo stuns its prey with a shock from its body
statement: The torpedo (electric ray) catches its prey by numbing it with a shock residing in its body, and can numb humans too.
quote: The torpedo narcotizes the creatures that it wants to catch, overpowering them by the power of shock that is resident in its body, and feeds upon them

label: Fishes have no pestilential diseases like those of man and livestock
statement: No pestilential (epidemic) disease is known to attack fishes as such diseases attack man, horses and oxen, although individual fishes do appear to fall sick.
quote: We know of no pestilential malady attacking fishes, such as those which attack man, and horses and oxen among the quadrupedal vivipara

label: Fig-wasps from wild figs enter cultivated figs and keep them from dropping
statement: The fig-wasp develops in the fruit of the wild fig, then flies into the fruit of the cultivated fig through its opening and makes the fruit stay on the tree, which is why farmers hang wild figs on fig trees.
quote: the psen leaves the husk behind it and flies away, and enters into the fruit of the fig-tree through its orifice, and causes the fruit not to drop off
scope: fig wasp (Blastophaga psenes) and Ficus carica (caprification)

label: Castrated cocks lose their crest colour, crowing and sexual drive
statement: A full-grown cock castrated by cauterizing the rump loses the colour of its crest, stops crowing and loses sexual desire; if castrated young, it never develops these male traits.
quote: If you burn this twice or thrice with hot irons, then, if the bird be full-grown, his crest grows sallow, he ceases to crow, and foregoes sexual passion; but if you cauterize the bird when young, none of these male attributes propensities will come to him as he grows up.

label: The trochilus cleans the crocodile's teeth
statement: When the crocodile gapes, a small bird, the trochilus, enters its mouth and cleans its teeth, feeding itself thereby, and the crocodile does not harm it.
quote: When the crocodile yawns, the trochilus flies into his mouth and cleans his teeth. The trochilus gets his food thereby, and the crocodile gets ease and comfort; it makes no attempt to injure its little friend
scope: Nile crocodile and the trochilus (a small Egyptian bird)

label: The cuckoo builds no nest and lays in other birds' nests
statement: The cuckoo builds no nest but lays its egg, usually one, in the nest of a smaller bird, after devouring that bird's eggs, and the host bird hatches and rears the young cuckoo.
quote: The bird eggs, but does not build a nest. Sometimes it lays its eggs in the nest of a smaller bird after first devouring the eggs of this bird
scope: common cuckoo (Cuculus canorus); hosts include the hypolais

label: Male sharks and dogfish have two appendages near the vent
statement: In cartilaginous fishes the male, unlike the female, has two appendages hanging down near the vent, and this sex difference is found in all species of sharks and dogfish.
quote: in cartilaginous fishes the male, in some species, differs from the female in the fact that he is furnished with two appendages hanging down from about the exit of the residuum, and that the female is not so furnished

label: Crocodiles enter water at night because it is then warmer than the air
statement: Crocodiles spend the night in the water because at night the water is warmer than the open air.
quote: for the temperature of the water is at night-time more genial than that of the open air.

label: Bees make wax from flowers but gather honey from the air
statement: The bee makes wax from flowers but does not make honey; it merely gathers honey that is deposited out of the atmosphere as dew.
quote: The bee, then, makes the wax from flowers. The honey, however, it does not make, but merely gathers what is deposited out of the atmosphere

label: Boys castrated before puberty keep a high voice; eunuchs never go bald
statement: Men castrated in boyhood never grow the later hair and keep a high-pitched voice, and a eunuch never goes bald.
quote: if you mutilate them in boyhood, the later-growing hair never comes, and the voice never changes but remains high-pitched

label: Embryonic parts form in succession, not all together
statement: The parts of an embryo do not all exist from the start; some are visible in the embryo while others are not yet formed, so they come into being in succession.
quote: That the former is not the fact is plain even to the senses, for some of the parts are clearly visible as already existing in the embryo while others are not

label: In all animals that move about the sexes are separate
statement: In all animals that can move about, the sexes are separate, one individual male and another female of the same species, whereas in plants they are combined.
quote: In all animals which can move about, the sexes are separated, one individual being male and one female, though both are the same in species, as with man and horse.
scope: Locomotory animals (contrasted with plants and sessile animals)

label: The smooth shark's embryo is nourished by a cord attached to the womb
statement: In the smooth shark the young develop with a navel-string attached to the womb, so that once the yolk is used up the embryo is sustained as in quadrupeds, with a chorion and membranes.
quote: the young develop with the navel-string attached to the womb, so that, as the egg-substance gets used up, the embryo is sustained to all appearance just as in the case of quadrupeds

label: Fishes have no organs or passages for hearing or smell
statement: Of the sense organs fishes have only eyes; they have neither the organs of hearing and smell nor any passages for them.
quote: with regard to the organs connected with the other senses, hearing and smell, they are devoid alike of the organs themselves and of passages indicative of them.

label: Children often inherit their parents' deformities and acquired marks
statement: Deformed parents produce deformed children (lame from lame, blind from blind), and children often inherit their parents' peculiarities, including marks such as pimples or scars.
quote: From deformed parents come deformed children, lame from lame and blind from blind, and, speaking generally, children often inherit anything that is peculiar in their parents and are born with similar marks, such as pimples or scars.

label: In most mating insects the female is larger than the male
statement: In most insects that copulate, the female is larger than the male.
quote: In most of those which unite the female is larger than the male.

label: Long pointed eggs hatch females, rounded eggs hatch males
statement: Long, pointed eggs produce females, while round eggs, or eggs more rounded at the narrow end, produce males.
quote: Long and pointed eggs are female; those that are round, or more rounded at the narrow end, are male.

label: In crabs and spiny lobsters the right claw is always the larger
statement: In the Carabi (spiny lobsters and crayfish) and in crabs the right claw is invariably the larger and stronger; only in the lobster is it a matter of chance which claw is larger.
quote: In the Carabi and in the Crabs the right claw is invariably the larger and the stronger.
scope: decapod crustaceans with claws: crabs, Carabi; lobsters (Astaci) as the stated exception

label: The bitch's gestation lasts sixty to sixty-three days
statement: Gestation in the dog lasts sixty to sixty-three days and never less than sixty, or if less the litter does not survive.
quote: The period of gestation with the bitch is sixty days, or sixty-one, or sixty-two, or sixty-three at the utmost

label: The hyena has only one kind of genitals, not both sexes
statement: The hyena does not have both male and female genitals; each animal has one, but both sexes have a mark under the tail resembling the female genitals.
quote: This is untrue, for the hyena has been seen to have only one pudendum, there being no lack of opportunity for observation in some districts, but hyenas have under the tail a line like the pudendum of the female.

label: Semen is always white, including that of Ethiopians
statement: Semen is invariably white, so Herodotus was wrong that the semen of Ethiopians is black.
quote: for it is also an invariable rule that it is white, and Herodotus does not report the truth when he says that the semen of the Aethiopians is black
scope: Humans of all populations, and animals generally

label: All animals are born head first in the natural course
statement: All animals are at first head-upward in the womb but turn downward near term, and in the natural course birth in all animals is head first.
quote: birth in the natural course of things takes place in all animals head foremost

label: All cetaceans are viviparous, never carrying eggs
statement: The dolphin, the whale and all other cetaceans (animals with a blow-hole instead of gills) are viviparous, carrying an embryo rather than eggs, as do humans and viviparous quadrupeds.
quote: The dolphin, the whale, and all the rest of the Cetacea, all, that is to say, that are provided with a blow-hole instead of gills, are viviparous.

label: The octopus changes colour to match nearby stones
statement: The octopus hunts by changing its colour to match the adjacent stones, and does so also when alarmed.
quote: It seeks its prey by so changing its colour as to render it like the colour of the stones adjacent to it; it does so also when alarmed.

label: The lion's neck is a single bone without vertebrae
statement: The lion's neck consists of a single bone instead of vertebrae.
quote: The lion has its neck composed of one single bone instead of vertebrae

label: Very few birds breed in their first year
statement: Very few birds breed within their first year.
quote: Very few birds propagate within their first year.

label: A pair of eagles needs a large territory and drives other birds away
statement: A pair of eagles needs an extensive area to maintain itself, so it expels its fledged young from the neighbourhood and does not allow other birds to settle nearby.
quote: The fact is that a pair of eagles demands an extensive space for its maintenance, and consequently cannot allow other birds to quarter themselves in close neighbourhood.

label: The heart is the first organ, a beating speck of blood
statement: The heart appears in the developing egg as a speck of blood that beats and moves as though alive, and two blood vessels lead from it.
quote: and the heart appears, like a speck of blood, in the white of the egg. This point beats and moves as though endowed with life, and from it two vein-ducts with blood in them trend in a convoluted course

label: Cranes migrate from Scythia to the marshes at the source of the Nile
statement: Cranes migrate from the steppes of Scythia to the marshlands south of Egypt where the Nile rises.
quote: for these birds migrate from the steppes of Scythia to the marshlands south of Egypt where the Nile has its source.

label: Bees carry a stone as ballast in high wind
statement: In a high wind bees carry a stone as ballast to steady their flight.
quote: In a high wind they carry a stone by way of ballast to steady them.

label: Female cartilaginous fishes are larger than males
statement: In the cartilaginous fishes (selachians) the female is larger than the male, and the same holds for most other fishes.
quote: In the cartilaginous species the female is larger than the male; and the same is the case with other fishes for the most part.
scope: selachians (sharks, rays, skates) and fishes generally

label: Men produce semen at about fourteen and are fertile at about twenty-one
statement: A man begins to produce seminal fluid at about fourteen years of age and becomes capable of generation at about twenty-one.
quote: Man begins to possess seminal fluid about the age of fourteen, and becomes generatively capable at about the age of twenty-one years.

label: Wind-eggs arise without any prior impregnation
statement: Unfertilised wind-eggs are not relics of a previous mating: they arise in hens and geese that have never been impregnated.
quote: Hence some are wont to speak of wind-eggs as not coming into being independently but as mere relics from a previous impregnation. But this is a false view, for sufficient observations have been made of their arising without impregnation in chickens and goslings.

label: Mutilated parents do not always have mutilated young
statement: The young of mutilated parents are not always mutilated, just as young are not always like their parents.
quote: And the young of mutilated parents are not always mutilated, just as they are not always like their parents
scope: Animals and humans with acquired injuries

label: Polydactylous quadrupeds bear blind young whose eyelids open after birth
statement: All polydactylous (many-toed) quadrupeds, such as the dog, lion, wolf, fox and jackal, bear their young blind, and the eyelids do not separate until after birth.
quote: Moreover, all polydactylous quadrupeds, as dog, lion, wolf, fox, jackal, produce their young blind, and the eyelids do not separate till after birth.
scope: Polydactylous (many-toed) quadrupeds: carnivores such as dog, lion, wolf, fox, jackal

label: Caterpillars feed and excrete; chrysalises do neither
statement: The butterfly caterpillar feeds and voids excrement, but once it becomes a chrysalis it neither feeds nor voids excrement; the same holds for all insects that develop from a grub, such as bees and wasps.
quote: At first, when it is a caterpillar, it feeds and ejects excrement; but when it turns into the chrysalis it neither feeds nor ejects excrement.

label: Women's skulls have one circular suture, men's usually three meeting
statement: The skull of a woman has one circular suture, while the skull of a man, as a general rule, has three sutures meeting at a point.
quote: The skull has sutures: one, of circular form, in the case of women; in the case of men, as a general rule, three meeting at a point.

label: Large animals have few young, small animals many
statement: Large animals have few young and small animals have many.
quote: A further proof that it is not a waste-product, but rather a secretion, is the fact that the large animals have few young, the small many.

label: The fishing-frog lures prey with filaments in front of its eyes
statement: The fishing-frog (angler) has long thin filaments with rounded tips in front of its eyes which it raises as bait while hidden in sand and mud, drawing small fish that touch them into its mouth.
quote: The fishing-frog has a set of filaments that project in front of its eyes; they are long and thin like hairs, and are round at the tips; they lie on either side, and are used as baits.

label: Only air-breathing animals are internally viviparous
statement: No animal is internally viviparous unless it takes in and breathes out air.
quote: for nothing is internally viviparous unless it receive and breathe out air.
scope: Internally viviparous animals (man, viviparous quadrupeds, cetaceans)

label: The heart is the first part to be distinctly formed in all animals with blood
statement: In all animals with blood the heart is the first part to appear distinctly formed in the embryo, being the origin of the blood-vessels and of the other parts.
quote: Therefore it is that the heart appears first distinctly marked off in all the sanguinea
scope: Animals with blood (roughly vertebrates); the heart's analogue in bloodless animals

label: Man is the only animal that laughs
statement: Man is the only animal that laughs, and therefore the only animal that is affected by tickling.
quote: That man alone is affected by tickling is due firstly to the delicacy of his skin, and secondly to his being the only animal that laughs.
